text:
toni: FYI I hit a weird TS friction in the new ESM samples for the SDK. Onboarding doc sample fails in Cloudflare Workers with our auth helper.

arjun: can you paste the error?

toni: short: `Argument of type '{ token: unknown }' is not assignable to parameter of type 'string | { token?: string; refresh?: () => Promise<string> }'`. Happens when D1.get or env bindings are strongly typed as unknown in the edge lib.

mei: this smells like the overloads we ship + unknown values from ambient edge types. TS chooses the first overloads and unknown won't satisfy string | { token?: string }.

toni: minimal repro I used:

```ts
// sdk/index.ts
export function makeClient(token: string): Client;
export function makeClient(opts: { token?: string; refresh?: () => Promise<string> }): Client;
export function makeClient(arg: any) { return new Client(arg); }

// src/worker.ts
import { makeClient } from '../sdk';
const c = makeClient({ token: ENV.TOKEN }); // ENV.TOKEN: unknown in edge types
c.request('/_health');
```

arjun: interesting. I think with `module: "esnext"` and `moduleResolution: "bundler"` the compiler does different overload resolution.

mei: also note TS 5 changed some inference around unknown in union contexts. When a property is unknown inside an object literal, the whole literal might not match an overload that expects a typed object.

toni: workaround: `const t = String(ENV.TOKEN); makeClient({ token: t })` or `makeClient({ token: ENV.TOKEN as string })`. Not ideal for docs.

arjun: we could change SDK types to use a discriminated single signature e.g. `makeClient(arg: string | { token?: string })` instead of overloads. That would avoid overload resolution quirks. Pros: simpler. Cons: less precise intellisense for callers who pass a refresh fn etc.

mei: another less intrusive option: add a final fallback overload that accepts `Record<string, unknown>` or `any` so the edge case of unknown binds to that overload and compiles. Eg: `export function makeClient(arg: Record<string, unknown>): Client;` after the strict overloads. Downside: slightly weaker type surface but only used for ambiguous callers.

toni: I like the fallback overload + onboarding note. We should also include a snippet in the edge guide explaining that some ambient bindings are `unknown` and recommend `safeString()` helper instead of `as any`.

arjun: +1. Also add a CI test: publish d.ts (esm) and then run a small sample compilation matrix with tsconfigs: module=esnext+resolution=bundler, module=es2020+resolution=node16, module=commonjs. That would catch regressions.

build-bot: queued job: ts-edge-typing-matrix (3 configs) :gear:

mei: nit: update our sample repo to avoid casting to `any` as a band-aid. People copy-paste examples and then accidentally suppress real issues.

toni: will draft a small PR: (1) add `Record<string, unknown>` fallback overload in types, (2) update edge worker sample to use `safeString` helper and a short comment, (3) add tsconfig matrix job to CI.

arjun: please also add a tiny test that asserts that TypeScript errors are emitted on a deliberately broken sample so the CI can assert non-regression.

toni: created ticket DX-1302 and marked sample-app blocked in docs until PR merges. Will ping reviewers when ready.

sam.dev: Thanks for catching this. Could we also add a note in CHANGELOG about the typing fallback so enterprise customers know the types change is intentional?

mei: yep will include changelog blurb. Also added a small example showing the preferred `safeString` helper: `const token = typeof ENV.TOKEN === 'string' ? ENV.TOKEN : String(ENV.TOKEN)` — avoids `as string` while still onboarding-friendly.

toni: posting the PR link when ready. Thanks :thumbsup:
